title: Host PDC never reported: plugin always claims zero latency while wet path carries limiter lookahead plus pedal latency
evidence: Grep over Source/ shows no setLatencySamples call on NOVAAudioProcessor; only OutputChain (OutputChain.cpp:187), ProcessorBase, and DryWetMixer internals call it
OutputChain always reports lookahead (~96 samples @48kHz) inside the graph; AudioEngine::getLatencyNumSamples() exists but is only consumed by tests and the internal dry-delay compensation
Tests assert graph latency invariants (AudioEngineTests.cpp:5670-5700) but never the processor-level latency the host sees
recommendation: Report audioEngine.getLatencyNumSamples() via NOVAAudioProcessor::setLatencySamples on prepareToPlay and whenever a graph publish changes latency (message-thread safe). Define dynamic-latency policy (live value vs stable maximum). Add a unit test asserting processor latency > 0 and equal to graph latency.

title: Auto-heal graph rebuild recreates pedals with default parameters; live pedal state silently lost
evidence: GraphBuilder::buildChain creates processors from GraphChainNodeSpec (type/zone/bypass only) via PedalRegistry::createPedal (GraphBuilder.h:188-239)

Pedal parameter replay exists only in SessionPersistence::rebuildEngineFromState (SessionPersistence.h:48-123), which is not invoked on the HealthMonitor-triggered RebuildGraph path (AudioEngine.cpp:302-310)
No test injects corruption and verifies pedal state survives auto-heal
recommendation: On auto-heal, capture live pedal states before rebuild and replay them after publish (or route the heal through the session layer). Add a corruption-injection test asserting parameter survival.

title: Global dry/wet mix applied after OutputChain limiter; mixed output not ceiling-protected at mix < 100%
evidence: processWithSampleAccurateDryWet mixes captured raw dry input with the graph output after runtime.graph->processBlock, which contains OutputChain (AudioEngine.cpp:557-596)
Only HealthMonitor's 24.0 linear hard clamp applies after mixing (HealthMonitor.h:50-113)
Dry component also bypasses InputChain gate/conditioning by design
recommendation: Decide policy: either move the global mix before the output safety stage, or apply a final ceiling after mixing, or document that the output ceiling guarantee only holds at mix=100%.

title: RoutingMixer remaps line gain <= 0.001 to unity: Level A/B parameter at 0 produces full volume with a discontinuity
evidence: RoutingMixer::makeLineTarget: 'target.gain = input.gain <= 0.001f ? 1.0f : input.gain' (RoutingMixer.h:66)
Host parameters Level A/B span 0.0..2.0 with 0.0 reachable (PluginProcessor.cpp:434-446)
Policy is pinned by tests AudioEngineTests.cpp:4762 and 5202 rather than challenged
recommendation: Decide explicitly: treat 0 as mute (preferred, continuous) or raise the parameter minimum. Update the pinned policy tests deliberately in the same change.

title: In-place active-graph mutation on pedal bypass: control thread calls graph->rebuild() on the graph the audio thread is rendering
evidence: applyPedalBypassToActiveGraph mutates slot state and calls runtime->graph->rebuild() plus latency update on the active runtime (AudioEngine.cpp:205-235)
Relies on juce::AudioProcessorGraph internal render-sequence locking; the audio thread can block on the graph callback lock during the swap
Test AudioEngineTests.cpp:5670-5700 requires in-place semantics (same processor instance across bypass)
recommendation: Measure audio-thread stall during rapid bypass toggling at small block sizes; if measurable, move bypass latency changes to the immutable-swap path or use a lock-free latency handoff. Otherwise document the lock contract.

title: AudioEngine::prepare() callable from message thread while audio callback runs; scratch/delay buffers resized unsynchronized (safe today only by ordering)
evidence: toggleEngine() -> hardRefreshAudioEngineForCurrentIO() -> audioEngine.prepare() from the UI thread (PluginProcessor.cpp:854-869, 982-1001)
prepareScratchBuffers resizes DryWetMixer scratch buffers and dryDelay vectors with no synchronization against process() (AudioEngine.cpp:412-418)
Currently safe because the engine is necessarily off at that moment, so process() takes the early-return path that never touches those buffers - an implicit, untested invariant
recommendation: Guard prepare(): assert or defer when isEngineOn is true, or gate buffer swaps through the same publish mechanism as graphs. Document the invariant either way.

title: InputChain auto-routing enters mono-copy mode after a single detection block with a hard channel copy and no crossfade
evidence: AutoRoutingDetector: transition from Stereo to LeftOnly/RightOnly is immediate (currentMode = detected, InputChain.h:221-227); only subsequent changes need 3 confirmation blocks
apply() performs FloatVectorOperations::copy of one channel over the other with no ramp (InputChain.h:246-259)
Asymmetric stereo program material can be collapsed or clicked at the base layer before any pedal
recommendation: Require confirmation blocks before entering (not just leaving) mono-copy modes and crossfade the channel copy over a few ms. Keep behavior for genuine single-jack guitar input.

title: Engine off/startup paths are zero-latency dry passthrough while engine-on is latent: toggling time-shifts audio with no ramp
evidence: Engine-off and startup-counter branches return the input buffer unprocessed (AudioEngine.cpp:504-519)
Engine-on wet path carries graph latency (>= OutputChain lookahead), so enable/disable jumps timing and level context without crossfade
recommendation: Optional polish: short gain ramp around engine enable/disable transitions. Low priority for a guitar-processor use case.

title: Audio-thread control work on engine-enabled parameter change: command-queue lock, deque allocation, SessionLogger string work, triggerAsyncUpdate from processBlock
evidence: processBlock -> refreshEngineEnabledIfNeeded(false) -> audioEngine.setEngineEnabled -> enqueueGraphCommand (CriticalSection + std::deque push) + SessionLogger::logEvent (PluginProcessor.cpp:551-558, AudioEngine.cpp:378-385, 241-253)
First block after prepare: updateGlobalParams triggers an async update because the audio thread ID is not yet latched (AudioEngine.cpp:190-192)
Steady-state path is clean; policy scan PASS (artifacts/audio-thread-policy-scan.txt)
recommendation: Defer engine-enable pushes to the control thread (set an atomic flag consumed by AudioEngine::run), keeping processBlock free of locks/allocation/logging on all branches.

title: True oversized-block fallback (wet-only path above 8192-sample scratch capacity) never exercised end-to-end
evidence: kMinimumScratchBlocks = 8192 (AudioEngine.cpp:17); shouldUseOversizedFallback only triggers above scratch capacity
The 'oversized' engine test uses kBlockSize + 32 = 96 samples (AudioEngineTests.cpp:5399-5444), exercising graph-larger-than-prepared but not the fallback branch
DryWetMixer fallback boundaries are unit-tested (4514) but not end-to-end through AudioEngine::process
recommendation: Add an end-to-end test with a >8192-sample block asserting wet-only behavior, finiteness, and no dry-delay state corruption afterward.

title: Dead safety code: resetRuntimeGraph never called; STARTUP_COUNTER_AUTO_HEAL and RECOVERY_COOLDOWN_SHORT constants unused
evidence: resetRuntimeGraph defined at AudioEngine.cpp:442-459 with zero call sites (grep)
STARTUP_COUNTER_AUTO_HEAL (Constants.h:102) and RECOVERY_COOLDOWN_SHORT (Constants.h:104) referenced nowhere; auto-heal path uses STARTUP_COUNTER_GRAPH_CHANGE via resetAudioRuntimeState(false)
recommendation: Either wire the auto-heal startup counter as intended or delete the dead members/constants to keep the safety surface honest.

title: Host parameter ranges exceed sanitizer ranges: bottom 24 dB of input-gain and output-volume knob travel is dead; output volume cannot approach silence
evidence: Input Gain parameter -60..+24 dB (PluginProcessor.cpp:427-428) vs sanitizeInputGainDb clamp -36..+24 (InputChain.cpp:3-9)
Output Volume parameter -60..+12 dB (PluginProcessor.cpp:448-449) vs sanitizeOutputVolumeDb clamp -36..+12 (OutputChain.cpp:3-11)
No test asserts parameter-range/effective-range agreement
recommendation: Align ranges in one direction (widen sanitizers to -60 dB or narrow parameters to -36 dB) and add a range-agreement test. Consider mapping the volume minimum to true silence.

title: Gate threshold of exactly 0 dB remapped to -100 dB (off): maxing the gate disables it
evidence: applyRuntimeParamsToGraph: 'if (gateThreshold == 0.0f) gateThreshold = -100.0f;' (GraphBuilder.h:120-123)
Input Gate parameter range is -100..0 dB, so 0 dB is a reachable host value
recommendation: Remove the 0.0 special case (the sanitizer and <=-95 off rule already handle defaults) or cap the parameter maximum below 0 dB.
